Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
Value Name: Sectoral requirements only (e.g., financial or telecoms data)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source URL was truncated/broken and unfetchable. Verified instead against the Data Protection Act 2019 (s.50) and its General Regulations 2021, plus the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner's 2026 cross-border transfer guidance: personal data processed for 'strategic interest of the state' — spanning civil registration/identity, elections, public finance, critical information infrastructure, basic education and healthcare — must be stored/processed in Kenya. This is broader than a single financial/telecoms sector rule, plus the Kenya Cloud Policy (2024) further encourages data residency across government generally. Revised up to code 4 (comprehensive requirements for broad categories).
